title: Can the Philippines become Southeast Asia’s next fintech talent hub?
summary: As demand for AI and digital expertise grows, GCash is helping develop Filipino talent through upskilling, career development, and academic partnerships.

blocks.text: As demand for AI and digital expertise grows, GCash is helping develop Filipino talent through upskilling, career development, and academic partnerships.

Editor’s note: This press release is sponsored by GCash and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece.

The Philippines has long established itself as a global hub for BPO and IT services. But as the demand for expertise in AI, cybersecurity, data analytics, and financial technology grows, new opportunities are emerging for Filipino professionals.
With Southeast Asia’s digital economy expanding, the question now is whether the Philippines can develop the talent needed to compete in the regional fintech industry.
For Robert Gonzales, Chief People Officer of GCash, the country already has a strong foundation. The challenge now is preparing its workforce for these changing demands.
The ever-evolving market is driving employers to seek professionals who can combine technical expertise with adaptability, critical thinking, and deep understanding of the business.

“Professionals must learn how to work with AI-enabled tools, interpret data, and exercise sound judgment when using technology,” he explained. “These skills are particularly important in fintech, where technological decisions can directly affect people’s money, their access to financial services, and trust in digital platforms.”
For Gonzales, the focus should be on preparing employees to work alongside emerging technologies rather than viewing AI simply as a replacement for human talent.

Developing a competitive fintech workforce also means investing in professionals who are already part of the industry. Through GCash Fintech University, the company provides upskilling and reskilling opportunities to help employees develop specialized capabilities and transition into new roles.

One initiative is the Solutions Architect Pathway, which trains software engineers and developers to become solutions architects. This is GCash’s way of addressing specialized talent needs through internal development.
“By turning adjacent skills into clear advancement routes, this program closes critical capability gaps while opening new internal career tracks,” Gonzales said.

Meanwhile, G for Growth, the internal mobility initiative of GCash, allows employees to explore career opportunities across different roles, business groups, and locations within GCash. The company also invests in leadership development through its Uplifting Leadership Program and diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives, knowing full well that building effective teams requires more than just technical proficiency.

GCash is also working with academic institutions to help prepare students for technology careers in the rapidly expanding fintech industry. For Gonzales, a stronger collaboration between universities and companies is essential to ensuring graduates enter the workforce with market-ready skills.
“The strongest partnerships are those that connect classroom learning with the actual challenges that companies and customers face,” he said.

Through its partnership with De La Salle University’s College of Computer Studies under the NextGen Tech Builders Program, GCash brings industry and academia together to support future technology professionals.
Another initiative, ImaGnation: GCash Innovation Challenge, gives students opportunities to apply their creativity and problem-solving skills to real customer challenges.

“Ultimately, we want graduates to enter the workforce with more than technical knowledge. They should understand how to solve real problems, work with different teams, and develop technology that responds to people’s needs.”

The Philippines may already have a strong foundation in BPO and IT, but with neighboring countries investing in their digital workforce, there’s a need to keep up with the changing demands of the industry.
The opportunity lies in nurturing talent early by harnessing the digital fluency of younger generations and turning that potential into world-class expertise in AI, IT, and fintech.

“Through our partnerships with academic institutions and continued investment in employee development, GCash is helping create pathways for Filipino professionals to stay globally competitive in the digital economy,” Gonzales said.

For GCash, these efforts are part of a bigger ambition of helping Filipino talent compete beyond the local market and positioning the Philippines as a potential fintech talent hub in Southeast Asia. – Rappler.com
